memo.headline: Put next quarter's effort into usability: it carries the heaviest complaint load of the four areas and holds the third-ranked issue, ads interruptions.
situation: The run labelled nearly all records, with only a handful quarantined, so the aggregates cover essentially the full review set.

Usability has the largest share of complaints among the four focus areas, ahead of billing_support, then playback, then access. Access is the smallest by volume but has the highest mean severity of the four.

The baseline ranking is led by other.general_negative, a catch-all of broad dissatisfaction that does not map to any one focus area. The second-ranked issue, billing.premium_only_controls, sits in billing_support. The third-ranked issue is usability.ads_interruptions.

top_issues.why_it_matters: It tops the baseline ranking on volume ({C1}) and priority score ({C4}), but mean severity is the lowest of the five ({C3}). It is broad dissatisfaction rather than a specific fault, so it gives product teams little to act on directly.

Reviewers object to features such as downloads and individual track choice sitting behind a paid tier. Complaint count is {C5} and priority score is {C8}, with higher mean severity ({C7}) than ads. It is the strongest single issue inside billing_support.

Free-tier listening interrupted by ads draws {C9} complaints, for a priority score of {C12} at mean severity {C11}. Reviewers describe ads after nearly every song and call it annoying; some also say premium is good, so the friction sits in the free experience.

Stuck offline mode, wrong songs playing and Android stuttering are core-function failures. Priority score is {C16} on {C13} complaints, with mean severity ({C15}) well above ads or premium-only controls.
Login errors and an app that will not open block use entirely, and this issue has the highest mean severity of the five ({C19}). Volume is the smallest ({C17}), giving a priority score of {C20}.

recommendation.argument: Usability has the largest share of complaints of the four areas, and its ads issue is the highest-ranked issue that belongs to a single focus area and is not a catch-all or a pricing-model question: {C9} complaints and a priority score of {C12}. Mean severity is moderate ({C11}), so the case rests on breadth, not on severity. Reviewers describe the specific friction (ads after almost every song), which gives the team a concrete surface to work on. The top-ranked issue, other.general_negative ({C4}), is too diffuse to assign.

alternatives.case_for: It holds the second-ranked issue, billing.premium_only_controls, with a higher priority score ({C8}) than ads ({C12}) and a second-largest complaint share, so it is a close contender.
alternatives.why_not_now: The complaints are largely about which features sit behind the paid tier, which is a pricing and packaging decision rather than a defect. It is a leadership call, not a product-effort workstream, and the review text cannot show how users would respond to changes.

alternatives.case_for: Playback complaints are more severe ({C15}) than ads ({C11}) and describe failures of the core listening function.
alternatives.why_not_now: Volume is lower ({C13} complaints against {C9} for ads) and the priority score is lower ({C16} against {C12}), so a quarter of effort reaches fewer complaints.

alternatives.case_for: Login failure has the highest mean severity ({C19}), and an app that will not open blocks the user completely.
alternatives.why_not_now: Access is the smallest area by complaint volume ({C17} complaints) and the lowest priority score ({C20}). It looks better suited to a targeted fix than to a quarter-long focus.

limitations: Reviews are self-selected public text; they over-represent unhappy and highly motivated users and cannot be read as the whole user base.
Severity and topic labels come from automated classification, and a sizable fraction of records was flagged for review, so individual labels may be wrong.
The baseline ranking multiplies complaint count by mean severity and does not account for user reach, revenue, churn or engineering cost, none of which are in the data.
The top-ranked issue, other.general_negative, is a catch-all category, so its rank reflects labelling breadth more than a specific fault.
The evidence pack contains only a few quotes per issue and is illustrative, not a representative sample.
